title: The great tongue (Kern ch. 20)
hook: the Buddhas show their power to confirm the teaching

segments.voice: Yesterday, Never Disparaging: the monk who bowed to everyone, stepped back from the sticks, and said it again. Your line: I do not despise you. Did the line get a chance to run? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-six.

A notary's stamp. A handshake in front of witnesses. A signature on the line, initials in the margin. People have many ways of saying: this counts, and I stand behind it. Chapter twenty of the Lotus Sutra, in Kern's numbering, has one of its own. The Buddhas put out their tongues. It sounds almost comic at first, and it is meant to be enormous. It's also the last day of this week, so after the scene we'll gather up the week's lines and see what today's gesture does to them. Today: the great tongue.
screen: `A STAMP, A HANDSHAKE, A SIGNATURE.` → `THE BUDDHAS PUT OUT THEIR TONGUES.` → `THE WEEK, GATHERED UP.`

segments.voice: First, the scene. The bodhisattvas who rose from the cracks of the earth have just vowed to carry the teaching after the Buddha is gone. Then Shakyamuni, and the ancient Buddha Prabhutaratna seated beside him in the jeweled stupa, and all the Buddhas gathered from other worlds, each on a lion seat, put out their tongues. The tongues reach up to the Brahma heaven, and rays of light pour from them. Tradition says a long, broad tongue is one of a Buddha's bodily marks, the sign of a speaker who does not lie. So the gesture is not rude. It means: what was said here is true. Second, the sound. Then the Buddhas clear their throats and snap their fingers, all together, and the sound reaches worlds in every direction. Beings everywhere look up, see the great assembly, and are glad. Third, the handing over. With the teaching confirmed, the Buddha entrusts it to the bodhisattvas. And the chapter says: wherever this teaching is kept, read or explained, in a park or a forest, under a tree, in a monastery or in a family's house, that spot is to be honored as the place where Buddhas awaken. Fourth, the week, confirmed. Look back at the lines you've carried. Always here. Take the medicine. Glad news. Passed on and on. Clear senses. I do not despise you. Each one came from a chapter of this sutra, and today the sutra puts its own stamp on the whole book, with a gesture as wide as the worlds.
screen: `TONGUES THAT REACH THE HEAVENS.` · `A COUGH, A SNAP, WORLDS HEAR.` · `ANY PLACE CAN BE THE SEAT.` · `A WEEK OF LINES, CONFIRMED.` · then, large: `CONFIRMED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: confirm one kind word with action. Sit and let the breath settle. Look back for one kind thing you said recently that hasn't been backed up yet. Let's get coffee. I'll call you. I'm here if you need anything. Hold it for a few breaths. Then let one small action come into view that would make it true: a time, a message, a step out the door. Let it get clear and simple. You don't have to do it now. Just let the breath rest around it. The bell holds the time.
The great tongue. In the Lotus Sutra, the Buddhas' tongues reaching the heavens, a sign that the teaching is true and confirmed. Today's word.
Your line: confirmed. Today, take one kind word you've said and back it with one action, however small. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-six.

howItsDone: Schools that center the Lotus Sutra read this chapter as the Buddhas' confirmation of the teaching and its handing over to the bodhisattvas, and honor the places where the sutra is kept and practiced.

original.note: Sanskrit: tongue; in this chapter the Buddhas' tongues reach the Brahma heaven.

trapdoor: what you thought: putting out your tongue is rude.
what it means: in this chapter it is the Buddhas' way of saying the teaching is true.

what a scholar hears: tradition counts a long, broad tongue among a Buddha's bodily marks, tied to truthful speech; the chapter turns that mark into a cosmic seal before the sutra is entrusted to the bodhisattvas.

notes: Paraphrased from Kern (SBE XXI, 1884), ch. 20; nothing quoted.
Week end (days 1170–1176): the teach looks back at the week's carries (always here; take the medicine; glad news; passed on and on; clear senses; I do not despise you).

Check: tongues reaching the Brahma world with rays; Prabhutaratna seated with Shakyamuni; clearing throats and snapping fingers; the entrusting; the list of places to be honored as the seat of awakening (bodhimanda).
Long broad tongue as one of the marks of a great man and a sign of truthful speech: framed as 'tradition says'; Keeper to confirm.
